data.content_ref: inline:The target's central claim asserts that 'the dilemma dissolves' via the eliminative default mechanism. Yet the target's own counterconditions enumerate as failure scenarios precisely the conditions that constitute the normal epistemic state of science: multiple unrefuted theories coexisting (countercondition 1) and varying costs of action requiring probability estimates (countercondition 2). These are not edge cases or boundary conditions — they are the typical situation in which the original dilemma arises. By listing the core problem as a countercondition while simultaneously claiming dissolution, the artifact is internally self-contradictory: it concedes the dilemma persists under normal conditions while declaring it dissolved. This is distinct from prior objections, which charged the target with an external gap; the fault here is that the artifact's own counterconditions refute its own headline claim. A dissolution that explicitly catalogs the standard conditions under which it fails has not dissolved anything — it has merely relocated the problem into its own exception list.
